newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent called slightly lower, gas oil off 50 ct.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent called slightly lower, gas oil off 50 ct.

text.p: IPE July Brent was seen opening five to 10 cents lower on Thursday after it traded lower on the Singapore market, while IPE gas oil futures were seen around 50 cents weaker after overnight U.S. weekly stocks data were deemed neutral to bearish, brokers said.
July Brent last traded at $19.18 a barrel on SIMEX in the early London morning, having closed at $19.24 in London on Wednesday ahead of publication of the American Petroleum Institute (API) data.
"The APIs were bearish to neutral. We had been expecting a build in crude stocks. Nothing exciting at all," a broker said.
"Runs were cut a little bit but they are still way up there at (API) 97 percent," she added.

The API report showed crude stocks up nearly 1.4 million barrels nation-wide. And though total gasoline stocks fell just over a million barrels overall, the decline in the Gulf (PADD III) was nearly matched by a build on the East Coast (PADD I) and there was a surge in gasoline imports to 600,000 barrels a day. Distillate stocks rose 3.3 million barrels overall.
"I think the APIs are neutral. Year on year, they are bullish but week on week they are bearish," another broker said, calling IPE June gas oil unchanged to down 50 cents.
Gas oil closed $1 a tonne up at $173 a tonne on Wednesday.
